item.name: Purchasing Vehicles and Equipment Through the Fleet Department

@graph.name: Purchasing Vehicles and Equipment Through the Fleet Department
@graph.description: A standardized process for requesting, approving, purchasing, and receiving new or replacement vehicles and equipment through the Fleet Department.
@graph.abstract: This procedure applies to City departments, the Fleet Manager, Procurement Division, and DPW Accounting involved in acquiring new or replacement fleet assets.
@graph.creativeWorkStatus: Active procedure; approval and effective dates not provided in source

audience.audienceType: City departments, Fleet Manager, Procurement Division, and DPW Accounting staff involved in fleet acquisition

@graph.yield: An approved, purchased, received, recorded, and paid-for vehicle or equipment asset

itemListElement.name: Initiate a purchase request
itemListElement.text: Begin the purchase when a department or division requests an addition to the fleet, or when the Fleet Manager identifies a vehicle or equipment item that requires replacement.

itemListElement.name: Review a new vehicle or equipment request
itemListElement.text: For an addition to the fleet, complete a New Vehicle Request Form. The requesting department and Fleet Manager review the request. Confirm the funding source before initiating the purchase.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The request is supported by both the requesting department and Fleet Manager, and the funding source is confirmed.

itemListElement.name: Confirm replacement eligibility
itemListElement.text: For a replacement, the Fleet Manager evaluates and confirms eligibility. If the requesting department and Fleet Manager agree, fund the purchase through the Vehicle Replacement Fund. The remaining purchasing steps then follow the same process as a new vehicle request.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: Replacement eligibility and funding through the Vehicle Replacement Fund are confirmed.

step.name: Issue the purchase order and secure the purchase

itemListElement.name: Request a purchase order
itemListElement.text: Once funding is secured, the Fleet Department submits a Purchase Order request to the Procurement Division. Procurement issues the Purchase Order, which serves as a binding contract.

itemListElement.name: Send the purchase order to the vendor
itemListElement.text: Send the issued Purchase Order to the selling vendor to secure the purchase. When the vendor accepts the Purchase Order, the order is confirmed and in progress.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The vendor has accepted the Purchase Order.

itemListElement.name: Turn in the replaced vehicle
itemListElement.text: For a replacement purchase, the requesting department turns in the old vehicle when the new one is delivered. Use a key-for-a-key exchange to maintain fleet inventory and replacement compliance.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The old vehicle is returned when the replacement is delivered.

itemListElement.name: Receive and enter the new asset
itemListElement.text: Receive the new vehicle or equipment at the Fleet Department with its invoice. Enter the asset into CAMS and assign a vehicle number to begin its service record.

step.name: Approve the invoice and process payment

itemListElement.name: Approve and process the invoice
itemListElement.text: Fleet approves the invoice and forwards it to DPW Accounting. Accounting processes payment and enters the asset information into MUNIS for financial tracking.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: Payment is processed and the asset is entered into MUNIS.

marin:responsibilityAssignment.description: Initiates requests, secures funding for additions, and turns in replacement vehicles.
Reviews and approves requests, confirms replacements, and oversees asset entry.
Issues Purchase Orders and manages vendor contracting.
Processes payments and enters asset data into MUNIS.

marin:retentionRequirement.retentionRule: Retain all purchase documentation according to departmental and City records retention policies.

@graph.name: 2026 Comprehensive Road Maintenance Operation Procedures
@graph.description: Consistent, safe, and efficient operational practices for maintenance activities conducted by the Marin County Department of Public Works - Roads Division.
@graph.abstract: This procedure provides a unified framework for planning, executing, documenting, and reporting road maintenance work to support public safety, regulatory compliance, asset preservation, and service delivery.
@graph.creativeWorkStatus: Active procedure; approval and effective dates not provided in source

sourceOrganization.name: Marin County Department of Public Works - Roads Division

audience.audienceType: Roads Superintendent, road and sign shop supervisors, maintenance staff, and contractors performing County road maintenance

@graph.yield: Road maintenance work completed safely, documented accurately, and communicated to the appropriate County staff

tool.name: Backhoes, loaders, graders, rollers, dozers, and paving machines
Mowers, chainsaws, chippers, pole saws, and vegetation equipment
Traffic control devices and changeable message boards

supply.name: Signs, posts, delineators, and striping materials

marin:safetyRequirement: Required PPE, including high-visibility vests, hard hats, gloves, boots, and eye and hearing protection

itemListElement.name: Pavement maintenance
itemListElement.text: Inspect roads for cracks, trip hazards, potholes, or subbase failure. Repair potholes with hot mix or cold patch, apply crack sealant where required, complete skin patches, edge repairs, or dig-outs, and ensure compaction and cleanup.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Drainage maintenance
itemListElement.text: Inspect culverts, ditches, inlets, curb, and gutter. Remove debris and obstructions, flush systems where necessary, repair or replace damaged pipes, headwalls, or grates, restore flow, and stabilize eroded areas.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Vegetation and tree work
itemListElement.text: Brush roadside shoulders, clear sight lines, trim vegetation obstructing signs, lights, or drainage, remove hazardous trees using proper procedures and equipment, and chip and dispose of vegetation at local dump sites.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Signs and striping maintenance
itemListElement.text: Replace damaged or missing signs, install new signs to County standards, maintain striping, markers, legends, and crosswalks, and clean signs obstructed by vegetation or debris.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Shoulder and roadbed stabilization
itemListElement.text: Grade shoulders to restore drainage, add aggregate or soil where settlement has occurred, and compact and shape shoulders for safety and runoff control.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Traffic control
itemListElement.text: Determine the appropriate traffic control under the MUTCD. Set up signs, cones, barricades, and flaggers; inspect the work zone before work begins; and monitor and adjust traffic flow as needed.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Storm response and emergency operations
itemListElement.text: Patrol roads during storms, report road closures, clear debris, fallen trees, and rockslides, perform sandbagging, pumping, and flood mitigation, assist emergency services, and document and report hazards immediately.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Slip-out response
itemListElement.text: Assess danger zones from a safe distance, install temporary traffic control, remove loose material when safe, install sandbags or k-rail as needed, and coordinate with engineering for permanent repair design when required.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Respond to customer requests and inspections
itemListElement.text: Respond to service requests in a timely manner, document findings and actions, identify follow-up needs, and communicate with the Superintendent or engineering as needed.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

itemListElement.name: Document and report work
itemListElement.text: Complete required records for daily crew activity, work orders, materials and equipment, incidents or near misses, storm activity, and photographs when applicable.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The work is completed safely, the site is left in a stable condition, and required documentation is submitted.

marin:responsibilityAssignment.description: Oversees implementation and compliance; manages budgets, scheduling, and priorities; processes invoices and time sheets; coordinates with Fleet and other divisions; supports supervisors and staff.
Direct crews; enforce safety and approve traffic control; review equipment logs and work reports; manage inventory; document events; and coordinate with the Superintendent.
Perform maintenance work, follow safety and PPE requirements, complete daily equipment reports, report hazards and work completion, and communicate with constituents and supervisors.
Comply with County standards, field direction, licensing, insurance, and safety requirements.

marin:retentionRequirement.retentionRule: Document daily crew logs and truck cards, work orders, completed tasks, material and equipment usage, incidents and near misses, storm activity, and photographs when applicable.

@graph.name: Airfield Inspection and Hazard Identification
@graph.description: Daily inspection and hazard-response procedure supporting safe airport operations.
@graph.abstract: This procedure identifies and corrects hazards affecting runways, taxiways, aprons, lighting, signs, safety areas, transient aircraft, and hangar rows.
@graph.creativeWorkStatus: Active procedure; approval and effective dates not provided in source

audience.audienceType: Airport personnel responsible for daily airfield inspections, hazard response, NOTAMs, and follow-up

@graph.yield: Airfield hazards are identified, addressed or communicated, and tracked through corrective action

itemListElement.name: Inspect airfield operating areas
itemListElement.text: Conduct a daily inspection of runways, taxiways, aprons, lighting systems, signs, and safety areas.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: All listed operating areas and systems have been inspected.

itemListElement.name: Check for hazards and operational issues
itemListElement.text: Inspect for Foreign Object Debris (FOD), wildlife activity, pavement damage, standing water during winter, obstructions, lighting issues, transient aircraft requiring tags, and conditions in hangar rows.

itemListElement.name: Address hazards immediately when possible
itemListElement.text: Correct or control identified hazards immediately when the condition can be safely addressed.

itemListElement.name: Issue required NOTAMs
itemListElement.text: Issue NOTAMs for conditions that may affect aircraft operations.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: Affected aircraft operators can receive timely notice of the condition.

itemListElement.name: Notify Airport Management
itemListElement.text: Notify Airport Management of significant safety concerns.

itemListElement.name: Track corrective action to completion
itemListElement.text: Follow up on identified hazards until corrective action is completed.
itemListElement.marin:completionCriteria: The corrective action is complete and the hazard no longer affects safe operation.

marin:responsibilityAssignment.description: Conducts daily inspections, identifies hazards, addresses conditions when possible, issues or initiates required notifications, and follows up.
Receives significant safety notifications and supports corrective action.

marin:retentionRequirement.retentionRule: The source requires inspection and follow-up but does not state a retention period.
